title: そChapter 2: Walking the Beaten Path Together 2
content: "I think that's how it is," I replied, considering that it might be the procedure.
"She is Erika Longdagger, and I am Shin Longdagger."
I swear, I really just stated our names normally.

I wasn't being bothersome, nor was I showing any anger, and I certainly wasn't trying to intimidate her. I might have had a slightly creepy smile when I mentioned Erika Longdagger, but I swear that was all.
However, the guild staff's reaction was unexpectedly enthusiastic.
"Longdagger! 'The Unworthy Longdagger'! So you really are the genuine Longdagger!"
What was with that overwhelming triple punch of "Longdagger"?
Suddenly, the guild staff member shouted, and I was suddenly filled with anxiety.
"The Unworthy Longdagger," Merseja had called me that too.
At that time, I had forgotten to ask what it meant, but hearing it shouted by a guild staff member from another country made me genuinely curious.
Could it be that my unworthy feelings for Erika had spread widely?
Well, I certainly thought my feelings were unworthy.

A second son of a poor viscount family falling for the beloved daughter of a marquis family, the Prime Minister's daughter no less—though I had never voiced it, it was clear to anyone that she was a high flower and completely out of my league.
They say the Adventurer Guild has its own information network.
Sometimes they even grasp details that the country itself doesn't know.
Could it be that even my unworthy feelings for Erika were known by that guild's information network?
Rather than being scared by the strength of the Adventurer Guild's information network, I was impressed.
Still, the fact that my feelings for Erika had spread even to another country... I felt so embarrassed I could die.
"Could you please tell me something?"
While I was surprised that my unworthy feelings had crossed borders, Erika stepped forward.
"What do you mean by 'The Unworthy Longdagger'?"
Huh? Is she perhaps angry? Erika's voice and magic power felt tense.
"Yikes!"
The female guild staff member froze at the direct confrontation.
"I am also a Longdagger, so if this is an insult... well, I will gladly accept it."
The guild staff member was sweating profusely.
I understood her feelings, but I wondered how appropriate it was for a guild staff member to act this way.
Adventurers are basically people who think of risking their lives and making a living through violence.
Moreover, I was just a sixteen-year-old, clearly younger than her.
If she froze every time someone was a little grumpy, she wouldn't be able to do her job.
Well, if Erika was angry, I would prefer to keep my distance.
"What do you mean?"
Setting aside what "what" means, her words were polite, but the temperature had dropped significantly.
"No, no, no! I would never say it's an insult!"
The guild staff's reaction was overly desperate, perhaps due to her panic.
"'The Unworthy Longdagger' is a famous title; there is respect and awe in it, but to say it's an insult is just not true!"
A title?
I tilted my head behind Erika.
Indeed, among adventurers, there are those who earn titles. My master is one, and so are my sibling disciples. But I shouldn't have had anything like that.
Those titles are something only special individuals earn.
It wasn't something someone like me, who had no distinguishing features, would have.
...Wait, does this mean that my unworthy affection has become so well-known that it earned me a title?
How embarrassing! What should I do? This is so embarrassing.
"Is that so?"
Erika said with a voice that sounded surprised.
The guild staff member nodded vigorously.
"Yes! Yes! It's already quite famous!"
Realizing that Erika's mood had improved, the guild staff member continued to speak rapidly.
Wait, are you going to explain the origin of the title with that momentum? That I'm so well-known for having unworthy feelings for Erika that it crosses borders?
I had to stop that, and I felt a sense of urgency, but the guild staff member's mouth wouldn't stop.
"'The Unworthy Longdagger,' the sibling disciple of 'Impaled Eluza,' and the disciple of 'Kind Barbara' is quite famous!"
...Huh?
I was perplexed by the sudden mention of my sibling disciple and master.
"They asked me to inform you that 'The Unworthy Longdagger' will be registering there soon, so please take care of them."
Ah.
I couldn't help but look up at the sky.
I had a pretty good idea of what was going on.
What are those two doing, threatening people?
I became an adventurer at the age of twelve.
It was a rather early age to become an adventurer.
Unless there was a compelling reason, normally, no one would think of becoming an adventurer at twelve.
I didn't understand at the time, but that's how the world works. Commoners could become bakers if they wanted, or lumberjacks if they chose.
Unlike me, they had many options.
So it was only natural that it would require a significant reason to decide to fight monsters with violence for a living at twelve.
In my case, I had none at all.
If I had to give a reason, it was simply that I wanted to be an adventurer—that was all.
My master said, "That was good."
A twelve-year-old child, clearly of noble birth, was approached by 'Kind Barbara' to become her disciple. This was before I knew my master was a monster at rank 9.
After a while, Eluza, who was the same age, became my sibling disciple, and for the next three years, I trained as an adventurer under my master.
Suddenly, while looking up at the ceiling, pinching my forehead as if to endure a headache, I sighed, and both Erika and the guild staff member looked at me suspiciously.
In truth, I felt a slight headache, but I spoke to the guild staff member.
"Forget everything those two said."
"Huh? Then you won't ask for special permission to register as rank 7?"
"I won't."
The guild staff member's face brightened a little.
"Even if you say that, if you refuse, wouldn't you threaten to impale all the guild staff?"
"I won't, and besides, Eluza wouldn't impale guild staff."
Her face brightened even more.
"Then, without special treatment, 'Kind Barbara' won't come to do her kindness to the guild leader?"
"I'm sorry, but that might happen."
The guild staff member thought for a moment, then muttered that it would only be the guild leader and sighed in relief.
Poor guild leader.
"I'm glad... I'm really glad... All the guild staff would like to express their gratitude to 'The Unworthy Longdagger.'"
The guild staff member thanked me with slightly teary eyes, but there was no way I was in a position to be thanked. On the contrary, I should be the one apologizing.
I didn't know what those two had said, but I was truly sorry.
While apologizing in my heart, I added for good measure.
"Also, I don't have a title, so you can just call me Longdagger or Shin. Even if I had one, it would be embarrassing to be called by a title."
The guild staff member tilted her head slightly at my words.
"'The Longdagger' has been officially registered with the guild, you know?"
"Huh?"

"It says here that you single-handedly defeated a pack of Shield Bulls at rank 1, a Lancer Python at rank 2, and a Needle Spider Queen at rank 4, all of which are indeed opponents that are unworthy of your rank. Furthermore, despite being a noble, you humbly sought guidance from commoner adventurers, demonstrating your high ambition. You truly are an adventurer worthy of the title 'The Unworthy Longdagger.'"
The guild staff member opened a book and read it fluently in front of my dumbfounded eyes.
"What is that?"
"It's the Adventurer Guild's directory. When a title is officially recognized by the guild, it gets published."
"I have no memory of introducing myself."
"It says here that the title was recommended by Barbara."
Hmm!
Hmmmm!
I felt an overwhelming urge to scream right now.
Victims of my master's kindness usually end up in this state.
I had rarely been in the position of a victim, but experiencing the effects of 'Kind Barbara's' kindness after a long time was quite a burden.
I suppressed the urge to scream. My face might have been slightly twitching.
"I see, thank you for telling me."
I managed to squeeze out my gratitude.

Once I understood the situation in the Adventurer Guild and the staff member's attitude, it all seemed simple. Even though it was in another country, it was due to my master, a rank 9 adventurer, and the unreasonable requests from my sibling disciples, who were already rank 7 adventurers.
No matter how high-ranked an adventurer is, it's only natural that they wouldn't threaten the Adventurer Guild unless they were a complete fool.
Of course, the adventurers would know that such a fool was about to arrive, and if two people who looked just like the rumors walked into the guild, they would definitely attract attention.
If a high-ranked adventurer was threatening... well, the guild staff would be scared.
What on earth did those two do?
I felt a serious headache coming on.
Erika was convinced that her impression of Shin was not mistaken.
To single-handedly defeat a Needle Spider Queen meant just that.
From his posture, walking style, and the way he carried himself, Erika had thought that Shin's abilities were certain, but she had to admit to herself that they were beyond her imagination.

To defeat the Needle Spider Queen meant he had either taken down the entire swarm of Needle Spiders by himself or had slipped through the swarm to defeat the Needle Spider Queen. This indicated a considerable strength even by noble standards.
As Erika was impressed by the strength of Shin that the guild staff had informed her about, she also had questions. Why was someone with such abilities completely unknown at the academy?
The academy's structure had changed with the times, but its fundamental purpose remained the same: to systematically teach combat skills to the children of nobles.
If one had sufficient strength, they would naturally be recognized, and it was common for nobles to showcase their abilities to elevate their family's status.
He was a strange person, but Erika found it "so like him." She didn't understand why, but she found it endearing.
While Erika was processing her somewhat unclear feelings, Shin completed his registration with the guild and handed her the Adventurer Guild card.
Commonly referred to as an adventurer card or guild certificate.
While she had known about it in theory, seeing it for the first time made Erika feel it deeply.
Ah, I am free, she thought.

She gently stroked the slightly resilient card with her fingers. Functionally, it was merely an identification card, but it was called an adventurer card, and in reality, it was a magic tool in card form. Most of its functions were for preventing counterfeiting, with the added bonus of being able to record names, current adventurer ranks, and monster subjugation records.
Naturally, her current record was empty; it only had her name written on it.
Erika thought again. Ah, this is just the beginning.
While Shin was glancing at the guild's bulletin board to see if there were any suitable quests, she realized she was smiling at herself.
It was an emotion that didn't suit her, and as Erika smiled wryly, she noticed Shin was being surrounded by other adventurers.
What was going on? Was there some trouble?
Once the misunderstanding was cleared up, the conversation progressed very smoothly.

As expected of the Adventurer Guild located in the city of Hekatai, Erika thought as she admired the bulletin board displaying the requests brought to the guild, only to find Shin being surrounded by adventurers.
The man had thick muscles and wore equipment made from monster materials.
In other words, he was an adventurer who had learned body enhancement at a certain age and had begun to earn enough to buy expensive armor made from monster materials.

Using body enhancement doesn't increase muscle size, so if someone has thick muscles all over, it means they have to have trained hard. According to what I learned at the academy, using body enhancement increases muscle density instead of size.
Thus, many commoner adventurers have large muscles.
Well, this might just be because there are many people who think of making a living through violence.

Conversely, slender adventurers tend to be the dangerous ones. My master is a prime example. He is a madman who chose to become an adventurer at a young age from among many other options. Whether he became one out of necessity or desire, the fact that he survived is already quite dangerous.
The man said.
"You've got some nerve pretending to be 'The Unworthy Longdagger,' the disciple of my respected 'Kind Barbara.'"
Seriously?
I was more surprised that my master was respected in another country than that someone doubted I was the real Longdagger. I was moved, more than surprised.
I instinctively pressed my eyes.
"Hey, hey! If you're going to get so scared you start crying, don't pretend to be 'The Unworthy Longdagger!'"
The man scolded me with a look of disbelief.
'The Unworthy Longdagger' is a burly man with a beard! For someone like you, who looks all soft, to pretend to be him is just foolish!
Who is that guy? I waved my right hand at the man.
"I don't know who that bearded Longdagger is, but I'll let my master know. He'll probably be really happy about it. What happens after that, I don't know."
Thinking he was belittling my attitude, the man's gaze turned sharp.
In that gaze, I realized that this man truly respected my master.
For an adventurer to look at another adventurer in that way within the Adventurer Guild means something.
As a disciple, I felt reluctant to let this escalate into violence.
I grabbed the man's hand as he lunged at me.
Shin's movements were beautiful even from Erika's perspective. I had always thought he had good eyesight, but with the difference in skill, it looked almost like he was predicting the future.

The adventurer who had attacked Shin probably didn't understand what had just happened. The man, perfectly read by Shin's flow of power, looked bewildered as he sat on the ground and stared up at Shin.
Erika could see that much.
What surprised her was what happened next.
For some reason, she found Shin and the attacking adventurer engaging in a cheerful conversation. Not just cheerful, but Shin was demonstrating the technique he had just used, gesturing animatedly.
Was that the flow of events? No, there was no way that was the case.
Erika felt like she was caught in some clever scam. Regardless of the man's abilities, his anger had seemed genuine.
Yet, before she knew it, they were laughing together.
A strange person, truly a strange person.
Erika assessed Shin as being quite un-noble-like.
"By the way, you seem to be quite the celebrity."
Erika said this as they walked toward the exit of the city.
"To single-handedly defeat a Needle Spider Queen is something we can boast about by our standards."
By "our standards," she meant the standards at the academy.
"Even if I say I did it alone, my master was there with me."

I said this to avoid any misunderstandings. I had indeed defeated the Needle Spiders alone, but that was part of my training with my master, who was a rank 9 adventurer watching from behind. I couldn't consider that my pure ability.
"Even so," Erika said, seemingly pleased to deny it.
"I'm sure you didn't let your master intervene, did you?"
In truth, I had no intention of letting my master intervene.
"So you either slipped through the swarm of Needle Spiders or wiped them out single-handedly?"
Erika spoke as if she were imagining that scene with delight.
"No, well, you see, I could only charge straight through while taking down the Needle Spiders."
I shrugged and replied to Erika's questioning gaze.
"I could only do that."

At that time, I couldn't have slipped through the swarm to defeat just the Needle Spider Queen, nor could I have wiped out the entire swarm of Needle Spiders. So I had no choice but to charge through the enemies in my path.
I remembered being laughed at by my fellow adventurers for being so clumsy.
"I thought I wouldn't underestimate you anymore, but it seems I still did."
"I'm not that great of a person."
"Oh? Are you being modest?"
Erika said this while peering closely at my face.
Her overly cute gesture made me instinctively turn away.
"I see, so you're just shy."
With that, Erika laughed.

Though there was a slight delay, we decided to head to the monster's first subjugation right after completing our adventurer registration, just as we had originally intended. We had gone to the Adventurer Guild early in the morning for that purpose.
By the way, it was Erika who suggested it.
She said it would be fun to live as real adventurers, not just in name, but I couldn't tell if that was just a convenient excuse for her to get through this farce or if it was her genuine feelings.
One thing I could say was.
"That sounds fun."
I murmured as I imagined Erika defeating monsters while setting the surroundings ablaze.
It was a grassland about two hours on foot from the city of Hekatai, using body enhancement.
I had casually chosen a request that asked for the subjugation of monsters that frequently appeared on the road from one of the farming villages supporting Hekatai's economy to the city.
It might have been too easy for Erika's first job.

The monsters sighted were a type called Bonbo, which had long claws and resembled monkeys. They typically formed packs, and their strength was about rank 2, making them relatively weak. Even I felt that way; for Erika, they were no more than pests.
The problem was.
Someone had neglected to teach Erika the concept of holding back.
Bonbo were monsters that often appeared in the grasslands, but their characteristics were having claws about the length of a human pinky and acting in packs.

When the Bonbo spotted us in the grasslands, they charged at us, but to put it plainly, they were about to see hell. From the moment they entered Erika's line of sight, pillars of fire erupted from beneath them, incinerating them.
And it was done simultaneously and accurately, targeting only the Bonbo's feet.
In my line of sight, about thirty pillars of fire shot up at once.
To me, who could see magic power, the swarm of Bonbo running toward us shimmered with golden magic power for a moment, followed by the cries of their demise—a hellish scene.
Perhaps it was the right timing for the swarm to gather, but I estimated there were probably just over a hundred Bonbo in total.
Erika sank that swarm into a sea of flames without allowing them to approach, whether they charged in a solid mass, tried to surround us, or attempted to sneak up using a decoy.
Bonbo are widely found in the Faltarl Kingdom.
They are weak, but they often attack in packs, leading to misunderstandings where inexperienced adventurers get hurt.
They are sometimes called "beginner killers," and despite their weakness, they are disliked by adventurers.
This is evident from the fact that they have a unique name, Bonbo, unlike many monsters with simple names.
But this time, they had picked the wrong opponent.
I felt a bit of sympathy for the Bonbo as I watched Erika wipe out their swarm in just a few minutes.
"Well, good job for now."
I approached Erika, who had turned the area into a sea of fire, though I hadn't let it spread.
It could be called a technique supported by incredible precision and magic power, but the sheer number of opponents had left bald patches all over the grassland.
The only area within a ten-meter radius of me that didn't have bald patches was around Erika.
"That was unexpectedly a lot of them."
She said, showing no signs of fatigue. On the contrary, she seemed satisfied.
She had probably used magic to her heart's content for the first time.

The power she had displayed at the academy was trivial compared to the hellish scene she had just unleashed. It was difficult to use magic freely at the academy due to the need to be considerate of others.
